title: Verify audit log entry creation on user login
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - User Login
  Scenario: Audit log entry is created when user logs in
    Given a user account exists in the system
    When the user logs in with valid credentials
    Then an audit log entry should be created
    And the audit log entry should contain the user identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the login timestamp
    And the audit log entry should contain the login event type
rationale: Audit logging must capture user authentication events to track who accessed the system and when, which is essential for security monitoring and compliance.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit log entry creation on user logout
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - User Logout
  Scenario: Audit log entry is created when user logs out
    Given a user is currently logged in
    When the user logs out
    Then an audit log entry should be created
    And the audit log entry should contain the user identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the logout timestamp
    And the audit log entry should contain the logout event type
rationale: Audit logging must capture user session termination events to maintain a complete record of user access periods.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit log entry creation on data modification
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - Data Modification
  Scenario: Audit log entry is created when data is modified
    Given a user is logged in
    And data exists in the system
    When the user modifies the data
    Then an audit log entry should be created
    And the audit log entry should contain the user identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the modification timestamp
    And the audit log entry should contain the data identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the modification event type
rationale: Audit logging must track data changes to maintain accountability and enable detection of unauthorized modifications.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit log entry creation on failed authentication attempt
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - Failed Authentication
  Scenario: Audit log entry is created on failed login attempt
    Given a user account exists in the system
    When the user attempts to log in with invalid credentials
    Then an audit log entry should be created
    And the audit log entry should contain the user identifier or attempted username
    And the audit log entry should contain the failed login timestamp
    And the audit log entry should contain the failed authentication event type
rationale: Audit logging must capture failed authentication attempts to detect potential security threats and unauthorized access attempts.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit log entry creation on permission change
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - Permission Changes
  Scenario: Audit log entry is created when user permissions are changed
    Given a user account exists in the system
    When an administrator changes the user's permissions
    Then an audit log entry should be created
    And the audit log entry should contain the administrator identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the target user identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the permission change timestamp
    And the audit log entry should contain the previous permissions
    And the audit log entry should contain the new permissions
rationale: Audit logging must track permission changes to maintain security and ensure accountability for access control modifications.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit log entries are immutable
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - Log Immutability
  Scenario: Audit log entries cannot be modified after creation
    Given an audit log entry exists in the system
    When a user attempts to modify the audit log entry
    Then the modification should be rejected
    And the audit log entry should remain unchanged
    And an audit log entry should be created for the modification attempt
rationale: Audit logs must be immutable to prevent tampering and ensure the integrity of the audit trail for compliance and forensic purposes.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit log entries contain required metadata
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - Log Metadata
  Scenario: Audit log entries contain all required metadata
    Given an action is performed in the system
    When an audit log entry is created
    Then the audit log entry should contain a unique identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain a timestamp
    And the audit log entry should contain the user identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the event type
    And the audit log entry should contain the resource identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the action description
rationale: Audit log entries must contain comprehensive metadata to enable proper tracking, investigation, and compliance reporting.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit logs are retained according to policy
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - Log Retention
  Scenario: Audit logs are retained for the required duration
    Given audit log entries exist in the system
    When the retention period has not expired
    Then the audit log entries should be retained
    And the audit log entries should be accessible for review
    When the retention period has expired
    Then the audit log entries should be archived or deleted according to policy
rationale: Audit logs must be retained for an appropriate duration to support compliance requirements, investigations, and historical analysis.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit log access is controlled
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - Access Control
  Scenario: Audit log access is restricted to authorized users
    Given audit log entries exist in the system
    When an unauthorized user attempts to access the audit logs
    Then the access should be denied
    When an authorized user attempts to access the audit logs
    Then the access should be granted
    And an audit log entry should be created for the access attempt
rationale: Audit log access must be controlled to prevent unauthorized viewing or modification and to maintain the confidentiality of sensitive audit information.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.

title: Verify audit logging for administrative actions
gherkin:
Feature: Audit Logging Rule - Administrative Actions
  Scenario: Audit log entry is created for administrative actions
    Given an administrator is logged in
    When the administrator performs a system configuration change
    Then an audit log entry should be created
    And the audit log entry should contain the administrator identifier
    And the audit log entry should contain the configuration change details
    And the audit log entry should contain the change timestamp
    And the audit log entry should contain the administrative action event type
rationale: Audit logging must capture administrative actions to track system configuration changes and ensure accountability for privileged operations.
generationSummary: Audit logging rule - Test cases for verifying that audit logging functionality is properly implemented to track and record system activities, user actions, and security-relevant events.
